1	# Search-R1 lite
2	
3	This is a minimal reproduction of [Search-R1](https://github.com/PeterGriffinJin/Search-R1) and an example of using multi-turn conversation and tool-calling in slime.
4	
5	## Environment Setup
6	
7	Use the `slimerl/slime:latest` image and initialize the environment required for Search-R1:
8	
9	```bash
10	cd /root/
11	git clone https://github.com/THUDM/slime.git
12	pip install -e . --no-deps
13	# for Search R1
14	pip install chardet
15	```
16	
17	Download and prepare the training data:
18	
19	```bash
20	cd /root/
21	git clone https://github.com/PeterGriffinJin/Search-R1.git
22	cd Search-R1/
23	pip install -e . --no-deps
24	pip install tensordict
25	
26	# Set your working directory
27	WORK_DIR=/root/Search-R1
28	LOCAL_DIR=$WORK_DIR/data/nq_hotpotqa_train
29	
30	# Process multiple dataset search format train file
31	DATA=nq,hotpotqa
32	python $WORK_DIR/scripts/data_process/qa_search_train_merge.py \
33	    --local_dir $LOCAL_DIR \
34	    --data_sources $DATA
35	
36	# (Optional) Process multiple dataset search format test file
37	# Note: the final file is not shuffled
38	DATA=nq,triviaqa,popqa,hotpotqa,2wikimultihopqa,musique,bamboogle
39	python $WORK_DIR/scripts/data_process/qa_search_test_merge.py \
40	    --local_dir $LOCAL_DIR \
41	    --data_sources $DATA
42	```
43	
44	**Note:** If you plan to use local search backend, see the [Appendix](#appendix-setting-up-local-retriever) for instructions on setting up the local retrieval server.
45	
46	Initialize the Qwen2.5-3B model:
47	
48	```bash
49	# hf checkpoint
50	hf download Qwen/Qwen2.5-3B --local-dir /root/Qwen2.5-3B
51	
52	# mcore checkpoint
53	cd /root/slime
54	source scripts/models/qwen2.5-3B.sh
55	PYTHONPATH=/root/Megatron-LM python tools/convert_hf_to_torch_dist.py \
56	    ${MODEL_ARGS[@]} \
57	    --hf-checkpoint /root/Qwen2.5-3B \
58	    --save /root/Qwen2.5-3B_torch_dist
59	```
60	
61	## Configuration
62	
63	### Search Backend Configuration
64	
65	The `generate_with_search.py` file supports both **local search** and **Google search** backends. Configure via the `SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS` dictionary:
66	
67	```python
68	SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS = {
69	    # ============== General Configuration ==============
70	    "max_turns": 2,
71	    "topk": 3,
72	    "search_concurrency": 256,
73	
74	    # ============== Search Backend Selection ==============
75	    "search_backend": "local",  # Options: "local" or "google"
76	
77	    # ============== Local Search Configuration ==============
78	    # (Only used when search_backend="local")
79	    "local": {
80	        "search_url": "http://127.0.0.1:8000/retrieve",  # URL of your local retrieval server
81	        "proxy": None,
82	    },
83	
84	    # ============== Google Search Configuration ==============
85	    # (Only used when search_backend="google")
86	    "google": {
87	        "api_key": "your_api_key_here",  # Replace with your actual serper.dev API key
88	        "snippet_only": True,
89	        "proxy": None,
90	    },
91	
92	    # ============== Log Probability Collection ==============
93	    "return_logprob": True,  # Set to True to collect log probabilities (required for TIS)
94	
95	    # ============== Reward Model Configuration ==============
96	    "format_score": 0.2,
97	}
98	```
99	
100	#### Using Local Search
101	
102	1. Set `"search_backend": "local"`
103	2. Configure `"local"` section with your local retrieval server URL
104	3. Start your local search server before running the training script
105	
106	#### Using Google Search
107	
108	1. Set `"search_backend": "google"`
109	2. Configure `"google"` section with your serper.dev API key
110	3. Get your API key from [serper.dev](https://serper.dev)
111	
112	### Enabling TIS (Trajectory Importance Sampling)
113	
114	TIS requires log probability collection. To enable TIS:
115	
116	**1. In `generate_with_search.py`:**
117	```python
118	SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS = {
119	    # ... other configs
120	    "return_logprob": True,  # Must be True for TIS
121	}
122	```
123	
124	**2. In `run_qwen2.5_3B.sh`:**
125	
126	Uncomment the TIS-related arguments in `GRPO_ARGS`:
127	```bash
128	GRPO_ARGS=(
129	   --advantage-estimator grpo
130	   --use-kl-loss
131	   --kl-loss-coef 0.001
132	   --kl-loss-type low_var_kl
133	   --entropy-coef 0.00
134	   --eps-clip 0.2
135	   --eps-clip-high 0.28
136	
137	   # Uncomment to enable TIS
138	   --use-tis
139	)
140	```
141	
142	And uncomment the TIS configuration paths in `CUSTOM_ARGS`:
143	```bash
144	CUSTOM_ARGS=(
145	   --custom-generate-function-path generate_with_search.generate
146	   --custom-rm-path generate_with_search.reward_func
147	
148	   # Uncomment to enable TIS
149	   --custom-config-path examples/train_infer_mismatch_helper/mis.yaml
150	   --custom-tis-function-path examples.train_infer_mismatch_helper.mis.compute_mis_weights_with_cp
151	)
152	```
153	
154	**Important Notes:**
155	- TIS requires `return_logprob=True` in `SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS`
156	- When collecting log probabilities, response postprocessing is automatically disabled to maintain token/logp alignment
157	- TIS adds computational overhead but can improve training efficiency
158	
159	## Running the Script
160	
161	```bash
162	cd slime/
163	bash examples/search-r1/run_qwen2.5_3B.sh
164	```
165	
166	## Code Structure
167	
168	To implement multi-turn conversation + tool-calling in slime, you only need to implement a custom data generation function and a reward model for the task. These correspond to the following 2 configuration items in the startup script:
169	
170	```bash
171	CUSTOM_ARGS=(
172	   --custom-generate-function-path generate_with_search.generate
173	   --custom-rm-path generate_with_search.reward_func
174	)
175	```
176	
177	These are the `generate` and `reward_func` functions in `generate_with_search.py`.
178	
179	## Appendix: Setting up Local Retriever
180	
181	This section provides detailed instructions for setting up the local dense retriever for use with the local search backend.
182	
183	### Prerequisites
184	
185	The local retriever requires a separate conda environment to avoid conflicts with the training environment. It uses GPU for efficient retrieval.
186	
187	### Step 1: Install Conda
188	
189	If you don't have conda installed, run the following commands:
190	
191	```bash
192	# Download and install conda
193	wget https://repo.anaconda.com/miniconda/Miniconda3-latest-Linux-x86_64.sh -O ~/miniconda.sh
194	bash ~/miniconda.sh -b -p $HOME/miniconda3
195	source ~/miniconda3/etc/profile.d/conda.sh
196	conda init
197	source ~/.bashrc
198	
199	# Accept conda terms of service
200	conda tos accept --override-channels --channel https://repo.anaconda.com/pkgs/main
201	conda tos accept --override-channels --channel https://repo.anaconda.com/pkgs/r
202	```
203	
204	### Step 2: Create Retriever Environment
205	
206	Create and activate a conda environment with Python 3.10:
207	
208	```bash
209	# Create environment
210	conda create -n retriever python=3.10 -y
211	conda activate retriever
212	
213	# Install PyTorch with CUDA support
214	conda install pytorch==2.4.0 torchvision==0.19.0 torchaudio==2.4.0 pytorch-cuda=12.1 -c pytorch -c nvidia -y
215	
216	# Install required packages
217	pip install transformers datasets pyserini huggingface_hub
218	conda install faiss-gpu=1.8.0 -c pytorch -c nvidia -y
219	pip install uvicorn fastapi
220	```
221	
222	### Step 3: Download Index and Corpus
223	
224	**Note:** The local retrieval files are large. You'll need approximately **60-70 GB** for download and **132 GB** after extraction. Make sure you have sufficient disk space.
225	
226	```bash
227	# Set your save path
228	save_path=/root/Index
229	
230	# Download the index and corpus files
231	python /root/slime/examples/search-r1/local_dense_retriever/download.py --save_path $save_path
232	
233	# Combine split index files
234	cat $save_path/part_* > $save_path/e5_Flat.index
235	
236	# Decompress the corpus
237	gzip -d $save_path/wiki-18.jsonl.gz
238	```
239	
240	### Step 4: Start Local Retrieval Server
241	
242	```bash
243	# If you encounter "conda not found" error, run:
244	# source ~/miniconda3/etc/profile.d/conda.sh
245	# conda init
246	# source ~/.bashrc
247	
248	# Activate retriever environment
249	conda activate retriever
250	
251	# Set paths
252	save_path=/root/Index
253	index_file=$save_path/e5_Flat.index
254	corpus_file=$save_path/wiki-18.jsonl
255	retriever_name=e5
256	retriever_path=intfloat/e5-base-v2
257	
258	# Start the retrieval server
259	python /root/slime/examples/search-r1/local_dense_retriever/retrieval_server.py \
260	    --index_path $index_file \
261	    --corpus_path $corpus_file \
262	    --topk 3 \
263	    --retriever_name $retriever_name \
264	    --retriever_model $retriever_path \
265	    --faiss_gpu
266	```
267	
268	**Important Notes:**
269	- First startup will download the model and load the index, which may take a few minutes
270	- Normal startup time (excluding downloads): 1-2 minutes
271	- GPU memory usage per GPU: approximately 5-7 GB
272	- The local search engine's Python process will not terminate when the shell closes
273	- To restart the server: `lsof -i :8000` to find the PID, then kill it and restart
274	
275	### Step 5: Start Training
276	
277	Make sure you're **NOT** in the retriever conda environment. If you are, run `conda deactivate`.
278	
279	```bash
280	cd /root/slime
281	
282	# Set your wandb key (optional)
283	export WANDB_KEY="your_wandb_key_here"
284	
285	# If ray process is stuck, try:
286	# rm -rf /root/.cache
287	# rm -rf /root/.*
288	
289	# Run the training script
290	bash /root/slime/examples/search-r1/run_qwen2.5_3B.sh
291	```
292	
293	### Troubleshooting
294	
295	**Ray process stuck:**
296	```bash
297	rm -rf /root/.cache
298	# If still stuck:
299	rm -rf /root/.*
300	```
301	
302	**Conda environment issues:**
303	- Make sure you deactivate the retriever environment before running training
304	- Verify you're using the base Python environment for training
305	
306	**Retrieval server not responding:**
307	- Check if the server is running: `lsof -i :8000`
308	- Verify GPU availability: `nvidia-smi`
309	- Check logs for any error messages
310

# Search-R1 lite

This is a minimal reproduction of [Search-R1](https://github.com/PeterGriffinJin/Search-R1) and an example of using multi-turn conversation and tool-calling in slime.

## Environment Setup

Use the `slimerl/slime:latest` image and initialize the environment required for Search-R1:

```bash
cd /root/
git clone https://github.com/THUDM/slime.git
pip install -e . --no-deps
# for Search R1
pip install chardet
```

Download and prepare the training data:

```bash
cd /root/
git clone https://github.com/PeterGriffinJin/Search-R1.git
cd Search-R1/
pip install -e . --no-deps
pip install tensordict

# Set your working directory
WORK_DIR=/root/Search-R1
LOCAL_DIR=$WORK_DIR/data/nq_hotpotqa_train

# Process multiple dataset search format train file
DATA=nq,hotpotqa
python $WORK_DIR/scripts/data_process/qa_search_train_merge.py \
    --local_dir $LOCAL_DIR \
    --data_sources $DATA

# (Optional) Process multiple dataset search format test file
# Note: the final file is not shuffled
DATA=nq,triviaqa,popqa,hotpotqa,2wikimultihopqa,musique,bamboogle
python $WORK_DIR/scripts/data_process/qa_search_test_merge.py \
    --local_dir $LOCAL_DIR \
    --data_sources $DATA
```

**Note:** If you plan to use local search backend, see the [Appendix](#appendix-setting-up-local-retriever) for instructions on setting up the local retrieval server.

Initialize the Qwen2.5-3B model:

```bash
# hf checkpoint
hf download Qwen/Qwen2.5-3B --local-dir /root/Qwen2.5-3B

# mcore checkpoint
cd /root/slime
source scripts/models/qwen2.5-3B.sh
PYTHONPATH=/root/Megatron-LM python tools/convert_hf_to_torch_dist.py \
    ${MODEL_ARGS[@]} \
    --hf-checkpoint /root/Qwen2.5-3B \
    --save /root/Qwen2.5-3B_torch_dist
```

## Configuration

### Search Backend Configuration

The `generate_with_search.py` file supports both **local search** and **Google search** backends. Configure via the `SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS` dictionary:

```python
SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS = {
    # ============== General Configuration ==============
    "max_turns": 2,
    "topk": 3,
    "search_concurrency": 256,

    # ============== Search Backend Selection ==============
    "search_backend": "local",  # Options: "local" or "google"

    # ============== Local Search Configuration ==============
    # (Only used when search_backend="local")
    "local": {
        "search_url": "http://127.0.0.1:8000/retrieve",  # URL of your local retrieval server
        "proxy": None,
    },

    # ============== Google Search Configuration ==============
    # (Only used when search_backend="google")
    "google": {
        "api_key": "your_api_key_here",  # Replace with your actual serper.dev API key
        "snippet_only": True,
        "proxy": None,
    },

    # ============== Log Probability Collection ==============
    "return_logprob": True,  # Set to True to collect log probabilities (required for TIS)

    # ============== Reward Model Configuration ==============
    "format_score": 0.2,
}
```

#### Using Local Search

1. Set `"search_backend": "local"`
2. Configure `"local"` section with your local retrieval server URL
3. Start your local search server before running the training script

#### Using Google Search

1. Set `"search_backend": "google"`
2. Configure `"google"` section with your serper.dev API key
3. Get your API key from [serper.dev](https://serper.dev)

### Enabling TIS (Trajectory Importance Sampling)

TIS requires log probability collection. To enable TIS:

**1. In `generate_with_search.py`:**
```python
SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS = {
    # ... other configs
    "return_logprob": True,  # Must be True for TIS
}
```

**2. In `run_qwen2.5_3B.sh`:**

Uncomment the TIS-related arguments in `GRPO_ARGS`:
```bash
GRPO_ARGS=(
   --advantage-estimator grpo
   --use-kl-loss
   --kl-loss-coef 0.001
   --kl-loss-type low_var_kl
   --entropy-coef 0.00
   --eps-clip 0.2
   --eps-clip-high 0.28

   # Uncomment to enable TIS
   --use-tis
)
```

And uncomment the TIS configuration paths in `CUSTOM_ARGS`:
```bash
CUSTOM_ARGS=(
   --custom-generate-function-path generate_with_search.generate
   --custom-rm-path generate_with_search.reward_func

   # Uncomment to enable TIS
   --custom-config-path examples/train_infer_mismatch_helper/mis.yaml
   --custom-tis-function-path examples.train_infer_mismatch_helper.mis.compute_mis_weights_with_cp
)
```

**Important Notes:**
- TIS requires `return_logprob=True` in `SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS`
- When collecting log probabilities, response postprocessing is automatically disabled to maintain token/logp alignment
- TIS adds computational overhead but can improve training efficiency

## Running the Script

```bash
cd slime/
bash examples/search-r1/run_qwen2.5_3B.sh
```

This section provides detailed instructions for setting up the local dense retriever for use with the local search backend.

The local retriever requires a separate conda environment to avoid conflicts with the training environment. It uses GPU for efficient retrieval.

### Step 1: Install Conda

If you don't have conda installed, run the following commands:

```bash

source ~/miniconda3/etc/profile.d/conda.sh

conda tos accept --override-channels --channel https://repo.anaconda.com/pkgs/r
```

### Step 2: Create Retriever Environment

Create and activate a conda environment with Python 3.10:

```bash
# Create environment
conda create -n retriever python=3.10 -y
conda activate retriever

# Install PyTorch with CUDA support
conda install pytorch==2.4.0 torchvision==0.19.0 torchaudio==2.4.0 pytorch-cuda=12.1 -c pytorch -c nvidia -y

# Install required packages
pip install transformers datasets pyserini huggingface_hub
conda install faiss-gpu=1.8.0 -c pytorch -c nvidia -y
pip install uvicorn fastapi
```

### Step 3: Download Index and Corpus

**Note:** The local retrieval files are large. You'll need approximately **60-70 GB** for download and **132 GB** after extraction. Make sure you have sufficient disk space.

```bash
# Set your save path
save_path=/root/Index

# Download the index and corpus files
python /root/slime/examples/search-r1/local_dense_retriever/download.py --save_path $save_path

# Combine split index files
cat $save_path/part_* > $save_path/e5_Flat.index

# Decompress the corpus
gzip -d $save_path/wiki-18.jsonl.gz
```

### Step 4: Start Local Retrieval Server

```bash

# source ~/miniconda3/etc/profile.d/conda.sh
# conda init
# source ~/.bashrc

- GPU memory usage per GPU: approximately 5-7 GB

- To restart the server: `lsof -i :8000` to find the PID, then kill it and restart

### Step 5: Start Training

Make sure you're **NOT** in the retriever conda environment. If you are, run `conda deactivate`.

```bash

# Set your wandb key (optional)

# If ray process is stuck, try:
# rm -rf /root/.cache

```bash

class QueryRequest(BaseModel):
    queries: list[str]
    topk: int | None = None
    return_scores: bool = False


app = FastAPI()

# The endpoint is a sync def, so FastAPI runs concurrent requests in a thread
# pool. Each search is already CPU-bound and internally multi-threaded (faiss +
# BLAS use many cores per call), so letting hundreds run at once oversubscribes
# the CPU and destabilizes the native libraries. Bound the number of concurrent
# searches; RETRIEVAL_MAX_CONCURRENCY (default 8) trades throughput vs. stability.
_search_semaphore = threading.Semaphore(int(os.environ.get("RETRIEVAL_MAX_CONCURRENCY", "8")))


@app.post("/retrieve")
def retrieve_endpoint(request: QueryRequest):
    """
    Endpoint that accepts queries and performs retrieval.

    Input format:
    {
      "queries": ["What is Python?", "Tell me about neural networks."],
      "topk": 3,
      "return_scores": true
    }

    Output format (when return_scores=True，similarity scores are returned):
    {
        "result": [
            [   # Results for each query
                {
                    {"document": doc, "score": score}
                },
                # ... more documents
            ],
            # ... results for other queries
        ]
    }
    """
    if not request.topk:
        request.topk = config.retrieval_topk  # fallback to default

    # Perform batch retrieval
    with _search_semaphore:
        tmp = retriever.batch_search(
            query_list=request.queries, num=request.topk, return_score=request.return_scores
        )

    scores = []
    try:
        results, scores = tmp
    except ValueError:
        results = tmp

    # Format response
    resp = []
    for i, single_result in enumerate(results):
        if scores:
            # If scores are returned, combine them with results
            combined = []
            for doc, score in zip(single_result, scores[i], strict=True):
                combined.append({"document": doc, "score": score})
            resp.append(combined)
        else:
            resp.append(single_result)
    return {"result": resp}

"""
Preprocess the QA dataset to parquet format
"""

import re
import os
import datasets

from verl.utils.hdfs_io import copy, makedirs
import argparse


def make_prefix(dp, template_type):
    question = dp['question']

    # NOTE: also need to change reward_score/countdown.py
    if template_type == 'base':
        """This works for any base model"""
        prefix = f"""Answer the given question. \
You must conduct reasoning inside <think> and </think> first every time you get new information. \
After reasoning, if you find you lack some knowledge, you can call a search engine by <search> query </search> and it will return the top searched results between <information> and </information>. \
You can search as many times as your want. \
If you find no further external knowledge needed, you can directly provide the answer inside <answer> and </answer>, without detailed illustrations. For example, <answer> Beijing </answer>. Question: {question}\n"""
    else:
        raise NotImplementedError
    return prefix


if __name__ == '__main__':
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument('--local_dir', default='./data/nq_search')
    parser.add_argument('--hdfs_dir', default=None)
    parser.add_argument('--template_type', type=str, default='base')
    parser.add_argument('--data_sources', default='nq')

    args = parser.parse_args()

    # data_source = 'nq'
    data_sources = args.data_sources.split(',')
    all_dataset = []

    for data_source in data_sources:

        dataset = datasets.load_dataset('RUC-NLPIR/FlashRAG_datasets', data_source)

        train_dataset = dataset['train']

        # add a row to each data item that represents a unique id
        def make_map_fn(split):

            def process_fn(example, idx):
                example['question'] = example['question'].strip()
                if example['question'][-1] != '?':
                    example['question'] += '?'
                question = make_prefix(example, template_type=args.template_type)
                solution = {
                    "target": example['golden_answers'],
                }

                data = {
                    "data_source": data_source,
                    "prompt": [{
                        "role": "user",
                        "content": question,
                    }],
                    "ability": "fact-reasoning",
                    "reward_model": {
                        "style": "rule",
                        "ground_truth": solution
                    },
                    "extra_info": {
                        'split': split,
                        'index': idx,
                    }
                }
                return data

            return process_fn

        train_dataset = train_dataset.map(function=make_map_fn('train'), with_indices=True)
        all_dataset.append(train_dataset)

    local_dir = args.local_dir
    hdfs_dir = args.hdfs_dir

    all_train_dataset = datasets.concatenate_datasets(all_dataset)
    all_train_dataset.to_parquet(os.path.join(local_dir, 'train.parquet'))

    if hdfs_dir is not None:
        makedirs(hdfs_dir)

        copy(src=local_dir, dst=hdfs_dir)

   - Multi-turn tool-use RL training (Search-R1 reproduction on Qwen2.5-3B using `slime` with Megatron-LM actor and SGLang rollout engines).
   - GRPO (`--advantage-estimator grpo`) with low-variance KL loss (`--use-kl-loss --kl-loss-coef 0.001 --kl-loss-type low_var_kl`).
   - Multi-turn rollout generation with local dense retrieval (`examples/search-r1/generate_with_search.py`, `local_search_server.py`, `retrieval_server.py`).
   - Token-level loss masking (`loss_mask`) for model-generated tokens vs. environment observation tokens (`<information>...</information>`).
   - Rule-based QA Exact Match and format reward scoring (`examples/search-r1/qa_em_format.py`).

3. Files and Code Sections:
   - `historical_evidence/manifest.json`, `outputs/metrics.json`, `outputs/historical_eval_trace.log`, `wandb/offline-run-20260821_033838-wi4fh8cz/files/output.log`:
     - Contains reconstructed and raw W&B logs from step 0 to step 199 (horizon 200 steps, `eval_interval=10`).
     - Shows `eval/nq_test` starting at `0.048` (step 0), rising to `0.1587` by step 69, and plateauing at `0.148–0.1657` (`0.1647` at step 199).
     - Shows severe response length collapse: `eval/nq_test/response_len/mean` drops from `1568.61` tokens (median `1049.5`, `truncated_ratio=0.3813` at step 0) to `14.13` tokens by step 59 and `9.76` tokens (median `9.0`, `truncated_ratio=0.0` at step 199). Training `rollout/response_len/mean` collapses from `1751.46` tokens (median `1099.5`, `truncated_ratio=0.40625` at step 0) to `~9–10` tokens (median `9.0`, min `7`) from step 50 onward.
     - Shows `rollout/zero_std/count_0` and `rollout/zero_std/count_1.0` are the only zero-std reward values logged, and `rollout/kl` in `data.py:193` logs `0.0`.
   - `examples/search-r1/run_qwen2.5_3B.sh`:
     - Launch script configuring `Qwen2.5-3B`, `nq_hotpotqa_train`, `num_rollout=200`, `rollout_batch_size=32`, `n_samples_per_prompt=8`, `rollout_max_context_len=8129`, `rollout_max_response_len=1024`, `eval_interval=10`, `lr=1e-6`, `advantage_estimator=grpo`, `use_kl_loss`, `kl_loss_coef=0.001`.
   - `examples/search-r1/generate_with_search.py`:
     - Custom multi-turn rollout and reward wrapper.
     - Lines 240-260:
       ```python
       obs_tokens_ids = state.tokenizer(next_obs, add_special_tokens=False)["input_ids"]
       response += next_obs
       response_token_ids += obs_tokens_ids
       loss_mask += [1] * len(obs_tokens_ids)
       sample.append_response_tokens(args, tokens=obs_tokens_ids, trainable=False)

       Here `loss_mask += [1] * len(obs_tokens_ids)` sets the mask to `1` for non-trainable environment observation tokens (retrieved passages / invalid action prompts) and `sample.loss_mask = loss_mask` overwrites the `0` mask set by `sample.append_response_tokens(..., trainable=False)`, while `rollout_log_probs` has dummy `0.0` values for those tokens.

     - Lines 156-209:
       ```python
       def compute_score_em(

           method="strict",
           structure_format_score=0,
           final_format_score=0,
           retrieval_score=0,
           format_score=0,

       ```
       `generate_with_search.py` passes `format_score=SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS["format_score"]` (`0.2`), but `compute_score_em` never references `format_score`, using `structure_format_score=0`, `final_format_score=0`, and `retrieval_score=0` instead. 97	def get_responses(
98	    logits: torch.Tensor,
99	    *,
100	    args: Namespace,
101	    unconcat_tokens: list[torch.Tensor],
102	    total_lengths: list[int],
103	    response_lengths: list[int],
104	    apply_temperature: bool = True,
105	) -> Iterator[tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]]:
106	    """Yield response-aligned `(logits_chunk, tokens_chunk)` pairs per sample.
107	
108	    After squeezing batch dimension and optionally applying temperature scaling, this
109	    function extracts the logits and tokens corresponding to response segments
110	    for each sample. When context parallelism is disabled, it slices directly
111	    from the concatenated sequence. With context parallelism enabled, it
112	    handles split sequences across ranks.
113	
114	    Args:
115	        logits: Model outputs with shape `[1, T, V]` (policy) or `[1, T, 1]`
116	            (value). Must be float32.
117	        args: Configuration containing `rollout_temperature` for optional scaling.
118	        unconcat_tokens: List of token tensors (prompt+response) per sample.
119	        total_lengths: Total sequence lengths (prompt+response) per sample.
120	        response_lengths: Response segment lengths per sample.
121	        apply_temperature: Whether to divide outputs by `rollout_temperature`.
122	
123	    Yields:
124	        Tuple of `(logits_chunk, tokens_chunk)` where `logits_chunk` is shape
125	        `[R, V]` (policy) or `[R, 1]` (value) and `tokens_chunk` is shape `[R]`
126	        (1D int64), both aligned to response tokens for one sample.
127	    """
128	    assert logits.dtype == torch.float32, f"{logits.dtype}"
129	    assert len(logits.shape) == 3, f"{logits.shape}"
130	    assert logits.size(0) == 1, f"{logits.shape}"
131	    logits = logits.squeeze(0)
132	
133	    if apply_temperature and args.rollout_temperature != 1.0:
134	        logits = logits.div(args.rollout_temperature)
135	
136	    cp_size = mpu.get_context_parallel_world_size()
137	    end = 0
138	    seq_start = 0
139	    for tokens, total_length, response_length in zip(unconcat_tokens, total_lengths, response_lengths, strict=False):
140	        if cp_size == 1:
141	            end += total_length
142	            start = end - response_length
143	            logits_chunk = logits[start - 1 : end - 1]
144	            tokens_chunk = tokens[-response_length:]
145	        elif args.allgather_cp:
146	            # DSA: global concat then contiguous CP split. Each rank owns logits for
147	            # global positions [chunk_start, chunk_end).
148	            logits_local_len = logits.size(0)
149	            cp_rank = mpu.get_context_parallel_rank()
150	            chunk_start = cp_rank * logits_local_len
151	            chunk_end = chunk_start + logits_local_len
152	
153	            prompt_length = total_length - response_length
154	            resp_token_start = seq_start + prompt_length
155	            resp_token_end = seq_start + total_length
156	            logit_global_start = resp_token_start - 1
157	            logit_global_end = resp_token_end - 1
158	
159	            s = max(logit_global_start, chunk_start)
160	            e = min(logit_global_end, chunk_end)
161	            if e <= s:
162	                logits_chunk = logits[0:0]
163	                tokens_chunk = tokens[0:0]
164	            else:

167	            assert logits_chunk.size(0) == tokens_chunk.size(0), f"{logits_chunk.size(0)} vs {tokens_chunk.size(0)}"

171	                total_length, response_length
172	            )

174	            logits_0, logits_1 = logits[end : end + chunk_size], logits[end + chunk_size : end + 2 * chunk_size]
175	            end += 2 * chunk_size
176	
177	            logits_0 = logits_0[logits_offset[0][0] - chunks_offset[0][0] : logits_offset[0][1] - chunks_offset[0][0]]
178	            tokens_0 = tokens[tokens_offset[0][0] : tokens_offset[0][1]]
179	
180	            logits_1 = logits_1[logits_offset[1][0] - chunks_offset[1][0] : logits_offset[1][1] - chunks_offset[1][0]]
181	            tokens_1 = tokens[tokens_offset[1][0] : tokens_offset[1][1]]

183	            assert logits_0.size(0) == tokens_0.size(0), f"{logits_0.size(0)} vs {tokens_0.size(0)}"

194	def _allgather_cp_redistribute(
195	    res: dict[str, list[torch.Tensor]],
196	    *,
197	    logits_local_len: int,
198	    total_lengths: list[int],
199	    response_lengths: list[int],
200	) -> None:
201	    """Redistribute response tensors from allgather-CP layout to zigzag ring-attn layout.
202	
203	    After allgather context parallelism, each rank holds a contiguous chunk of
204	    the global sequence.  This helper reconstructs per-sample full response
205	    tensors via a differentiable all-reduce and re-slices them into the zigzag
206	    CP pattern expected by downstream code.
207	
208	    The *res* dict is modified **in-place**.
209	
210	    Args:
211	        res: Dict mapping metric names to lists of per-sample tensors.
212	        logits_local_len: Local sequence length on this rank.
213	        total_lengths: Total sequence lengths (prompt + response) per sample.
214	        response_lengths: Response segment lengths per sample.
215	    """
216	    cp_group = mpu.get_context_parallel_group()
217	    cp_rank = mpu.get_context_parallel_rank()
218	    chunk_start = cp_rank * logits_local_len
219	    chunk_end = chunk_start + logits_local_len
220	
221	    for key, values in res.items():
222	        # Skip keys where all values are None (e.g. entropy when not computed)
223	        if all(v is None for v in values):
224	            continue
225	
226	        # Determine reference dtype/device from first non-None value
227	        ref_value = next(v for v in values if v is not None)
228	        ref_dtype = ref_value.dtype
229	        ref_device = ref_value.device
230	
231	        # Reconstruct full response tensors with each rank's contiguous contribution
232	        full_resps = []
233	        seq_start = 0
234	        for value, total_length, response_length in zip(values, total_lengths, response_lengths, strict=False):
235	            prompt_length = total_length - response_length
236	            logit_global_start = seq_start + prompt_length - 1
237	            logit_global_end = seq_start + total_length - 1
238	
239	            s = max(logit_global_start, chunk_start)
240	            e = min(logit_global_end, chunk_end)
241	
242	            if value is None or e <= s:
243	                # This rank has no response logprobs for this sample
244	                full_resp = torch.zeros(
245	                    response_length,
246	                    dtype=ref_dtype,
247	                    device=ref_device,
248	                    requires_grad=ref_value.requires_grad,
249	                )
250	            else:
251	                resp_start = s - logit_global_start
252	                resp_end = e - logit_global_start
253	                full_resp = F.pad(value, (resp_start, response_length - resp_end))
254	
255	            assert full_resp.size(0) == response_length, f"Expected {response_length}, got {full_resp.size(0)}"
256	            full_resps.append(full_resp)
257	            seq_start += total_length
258	
259	        # Single differentiable all-reduce to gather full response from all CP ranks.
260	        all_cat = torch.cat(full_resps, dim=0)
261	        all_cat = dist.nn.all_reduce(all_cat, group=cp_group)
262	
263	        # Re-slice each sample into zigzag CP pattern
264	        new_values = []
265	        for full_resp, total_length, response_length in zip(
266	            all_cat.split(response_lengths, dim=0), total_lengths, response_lengths, strict=False
267	        ):
268	            new_values.append(slice_log_prob_with_cp(full_resp, total_length, response_length))
269	
270	        res[key] = new_values

273	def _build_shifted_tokens(
274	    T: int,
275	    device: torch.device,
276	    unconcat_tokens: list[torch.Tensor],
277	    total_lengths: list[int],
278	    response_lengths: list[int],
279	    allgather_cp: bool,
280	) -> torch.Tensor:
281	    """Build shifted target tokens for the full packed/padded logits."""
282	    cp_size = mpu.get_context_parallel_world_size()
283	
284	    # --- zigzag CP: completely different layout ---
285	    if cp_size > 1 and not allgather_cp:
286	        full_tokens = torch.zeros(T, dtype=torch.long, device=device)
287	        end = 0
288	        for tokens, total_length, response_length in zip(
289	            unconcat_tokens, total_lengths, response_lengths, strict=False
290	        ):
291	            chunk_size_cp, chunks_offset, logits_offset, tokens_offset = get_logits_and_tokens_offset_with_cp(
292	                total_length, response_length
293	            )
294	            for half, base in ((0, end), (1, end + chunk_size_cp)):
295	                lo = logits_offset[half][0] - chunks_offset[half][0]
296	                hi = logits_offset[half][1] - chunks_offset[half][0]
297	                full_tokens[base + lo : base + hi] = tokens[tokens_offset[half][0] : tokens_offset[half][1]]
298	            end += 2 * chunk_size_cp
299	        return full_tokens

from argparse import Namespace
from collections.abc import Callable, Iterator
from typing import Any

import torch
import torch.distributed as dist
import torch.nn.functional as F
from megatron.core import mpu
from torch.utils.checkpoint import checkpoint

from slime.utils.distributed_utils import distributed_masked_whiten
from slime.utils.misc import load_function
from slime.utils.ppo_utils import (
    calculate_log_probs_and_entropy,
    compute_approx_kl,
    compute_cispo_loss,
    compute_gspo_kl,
    compute_opsm_mask,
    compute_policy_loss,
    get_advantages_and_returns_batch,
    get_grpo_returns,
    get_reinforce_plus_plus_baseline_advantages,
    get_reinforce_plus_plus_returns,
)
from slime.utils.types import RolloutBatch

from .cp_utils import (
    all_gather_with_cp,
    get_logits_and_tokens_offset_with_cp,
    get_sum_of_sample_mean,
    slice_log_prob_with_cp,
)

ROLLOUT_TOP_P_TOKEN_KEYS = (
    "rollout_top_p_token_ids",
    "rollout_top_p_token_offsets",
)


# Optional capture of per-sample policy log-probs computed during the training
# forward. Used only when dumping train debug data in configs that skip the
# separate log-prob recompute (can_reuse_log_probs_in_loss / use_rollout_logprobs):
# the values are identical to a separate compute_log_prob pass, so we snapshot
# them here at no extra forward. Keyed by GLOBAL rollout position so the writer
# can put them back in sample order regardless of pipeline/microbatch order.
_LOG_PROB_CAPTURE: "dict[int, torch.Tensor] | None" = None


def enable_log_prob_capture() -> None:
    """Start capturing training-forward log-probs (call before ``train``)."""
    global _LOG_PROB_CAPTURE
    _LOG_PROB_CAPTURE = {}


def drain_captured_log_probs() -> "dict[int, torch.Tensor]":
    """Return captured ``{rollout_position: cp-local log_probs}`` and stop capturing."""
    global _LOG_PROB_CAPTURE
    captured = _LOG_PROB_CAPTURE or {}
    _LOG_PROB_CAPTURE = None
    return captured


def _maybe_capture_log_probs(batch: RolloutBatch, log_probs: list[torch.Tensor]) -> None:
    """Snapshot per-sample CP-local ``log_probs`` keyed by global rollout position.

    No-op unless :func:`enable_log_prob_capture` is active and the micro-batch
    carries ``partition`` (only added to the training keys when dumping). First
    occurrence per position wins, so multi-step training keeps the initial
    (old-policy) values. ``log_probs`` here is the per-sample list, in the same
    order as ``batch['partition']`` (both indexed by this micro-batch's
    ``micro_batch_indices``).
    """
    if _LOG_PROB_CAPTURE is None:
        return
    positions = batch.get("partition")
    if not positions:
        return
    for position, log_prob in zip(positions, log_probs, strict=True):
        if position not in _LOG_PROB_CAPTURE:
            _LOG_PROB_CAPTURE[position] = log_prob.detach().clone()


def get_rollout_top_p_logprob_kwargs(args: Namespace, batch: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    if args.rollout_top_p == 1.0:
        return {}

    top_p_token_ids = batch.get("rollout_top_p_token_ids")
    top_p_token_offsets = batch.get("rollout_top_p_token_offsets")
    if top_p_token_ids is None or top_p_token_offsets is None:
        raise ValueError("rollout_top_p != 1.0 requires rollout_top_p_token_ids and rollout_top_p_token_offsets.")
    return {
        "top_p_token_ids": top_p_token_ids,
        "top_p_token_offsets": top_p_token_offsets,
    }


def get_responses(
    logits: torch.Tensor,
    *,
    args: Namespace,
    unconcat_tokens: list[torch.Tensor],
    total_lengths: list[int],
    response_lengths: list[int],
    apply_temperature: bool = True,
) -> Iterator[tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]]:
    """Yield response-aligned `(logits_chunk, tokens_chunk)` pairs per sample.

    After squeezing batch dimension and optionally applying temperature scaling, this
    function extracts the logits and tokens corresponding to response segments
    for each sample. When context parallelism is disabled, it slices directly
    from the concatenated sequence. With context parallelism enabled, it
    handles split sequences across ranks.

    Args:
        logits: Model outputs with shape `[1, T, V]` (policy) or `[1, T, 1]`
            (value). Must be float32.
        args: Configuration containing `rollout_temperature` for optional scaling.
        unconcat_tokens: List of token tensors (prompt+response) per sample.
        total_lengths: Total sequence lengths (prompt+response) per sample.
        response_lengths: Response segment lengths per sample.
        apply_temperature: Whether to divide outputs by `rollout_temperature`.

    Yields:
        Tuple of `(logits_chunk, tokens_chunk)` where `logits_chunk` is shape
        `[R, V]` (policy) or `[R, 1]` (value) and `tokens_chunk` is shape `[R]`
        (1D int64), both aligned to response tokens for one sample.
    """
    assert logits.dtype == torch.float32, f"{logits.dtype}"
    assert len(logits.shape) == 3, f"{logits.shape}"
    assert logits.size(0) == 1, f"{logits.shape}"
    logits = logits.squeeze(0)

    if apply_temperature and args.rollout_temperature != 1.0:
        logits = logits.div(args.rollout_temperature)

    cp_size = mpu.get_context_parallel_world_size()
    end = 0
    seq_start = 0
    for tokens, total_length, response_length in zip(unconcat_tokens, total_lengths, response_lengths, strict=False):
        if cp_size == 1:
            end += total_length
            start = end - response_length
            logits_chunk = logits[start - 1 : end - 1]
            tokens_chunk = tokens[-response_length:]
        elif args.allgather_cp:
            # DSA: global concat then contiguous CP split. Each rank owns logits for
            # global positions [chunk_start, chunk_end).
            logits_local_len = logits.size(0)
            cp_rank = mpu.get_context_parallel_rank()
            chunk_start = cp_rank * logits_local_len
            chunk_end = chunk_start + logits_local_len

            prompt_length = total_length - response_length
            resp_token_start = seq_start + prompt_length
            resp_token_end = seq_start + total_length
            logit_global_start = resp_token_start - 1
            logit_global_end = resp_token_end - 1

            s = max(logit_global_start, chunk_start)
            e = min(logit_global_end, chunk_end)
            if e <= s:
                logits_chunk = logits[0:0]
                tokens_chunk = tokens[0:0]
            else:
                logits_chunk = logits[s - chunk_start : e - chunk_start]
                tokens_chunk = tokens[(s + 1) - seq_start : (e + 1) - seq_start]
            assert logits_chunk.size(0) == tokens_chunk.size(0), f"{logits_chunk.size(0)} vs {tokens_chunk.size(0)}"
        else:
            # TODO: this is super ugly... do better abstraction.
            chunk_size, chunks_offset, logits_offset, tokens_offset = get_logits_and_tokens_offset_with_cp(
                total_length, response_length
            )

            logits_0, logits_1 = logits[end : end + chunk_size], logits[end + chunk_size : end + 2 * chunk_size]
            end += 2 * chunk_size

            logits_0 = logits_0[logits_offset[0][0] - chunks_offset[0][0] : logits_offset[0][1] - chunks_offset[0][0]]
            tokens_0 = tokens[tokens_offset[0][0] : tokens_offset[0][1]]

            logits_1 = logits_1[logits_offset[1][0] - chunks_offset[1][0] : logits_offset[1][1] - chunks_offset[1][0]]
            tokens_1 = tokens[tokens_offset[1][0] : tokens_offset[1][1]]

            assert logits_0.size(0) == tokens_0.size(0), f"{logits_0.size(0)} vs {tokens_0.size(0)}"
            assert logits_1.size(0) == tokens_1.size(0), f"{logits_1.size(0)} vs {tokens_1.size(0)}"

            logits_chunk = torch.cat([logits_0, logits_1], dim=0)
            tokens_chunk = torch.cat([tokens_0, tokens_1], dim=0)

        seq_start += total_length

        yield logits_chunk, tokens_chunk


def _allgather_cp_redistribute(
    res: dict[str, list[torch.Tensor]],
    *,
    logits_local_len: int,
    total_lengths: list[int],
    response_lengths: list[int],
) -> None:
    """Redistribute response tensors from allgather-CP layout to zigzag ring-attn layout.

    After allgather context parallelism, each rank holds a contiguous chunk of
    the global sequence.  This helper reconstructs per-sample full response
    tensors via a differentiable all-reduce and re-slices them into the zigzag
    CP pattern expected by downstream code.

    The *res* dict is modified **in-place**.

    Args:
        res: Dict mapping metric names to lists of per-sample tensors.
        logits_local_len: Local sequence length on this rank.
        total_lengths: Total sequence lengths (prompt + response) per sample.
        response_lengths: Response segment lengths per sample.
    """
    cp_group = mpu.get_context_parallel_group()
    cp_rank = mpu.get_context_parallel_rank()
    chunk_start = cp_rank * logits_local_len
    chunk_end = chunk_start + logits_local_len

    for key, values in res.items():
        # Skip keys where all values are None (e.g. entropy when not computed)
        if all(v is None for v in values):
            continue

        # Determine reference dtype/device from first non-None value
        ref_value = next(v for v in values if v is not None)
        ref_dtype = ref_value.dtype
        ref_device = ref_value.device

        # Reconstruct full response tensors with each rank's contiguous contribution
        full_resps = []
        seq_start = 0
        for value, total_length, response_length in zip(values, total_lengths, response_lengths, strict=False):
            prompt_length = total_length - response_length
            logit_global_start = seq_start + prompt_length - 1
            logit_global_end = seq_start + total_length - 1

            s = max(logit_global_start, chunk_start)
            e = min(logit_global_end, chunk_end)

            if value is None or e <= s:
                # This rank has no response logprobs for this sample
                full_resp = torch.zeros(
                    response_length,
                    dtype=ref_dtype,
                    device=ref_device,
                    requires_grad=ref_value.requires_grad,
                )
            else:
                resp_start = s - logit_global_start
                resp_end = e - logit_global_start
                full_resp = F.pad(value, (resp_start, response_length - resp_end))

            assert full_resp.size(0) == response_length, f"Expected {response_length}, got {full_resp.size(0)}"
            full_resps.append(full_resp)
            seq_start += total_length

        # Single differentiable all-reduce to gather full response from all CP ranks.
        all_cat = torch.cat(full_resps, dim=0)
        all_cat = dist.nn.all_reduce(all_cat, group=cp_group)

        # Re-slice each sample into zigzag CP pattern
        new_values = []
        for full_resp, total_length, response_length in zip(
            all_cat.split(response_lengths, dim=0), total_lengths, response_lengths, strict=False
        ):
            new_values.append(slice_log_prob_with_cp(full_resp, total_length, response_length))

        res[key] = new_values


def _build_shifted_tokens(
    T: int,
    device: torch.device,
    unconcat_tokens: list[torch.Tensor],
    total_lengths: list[int],
    response_lengths: list[int],
    allgather_cp: bool,
) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Build shifted target tokens for the full packed/padded logits."""
    cp_size = mpu.get_context_parallel_world_size()

    # --- zigzag CP: completely different layout ---
    if cp_size > 1 and not allgather_cp:
        full_tokens = torch.zeros(T, dtype=torch.long, device=device)
        end = 0
        for tokens, total_length, response_length in zip(
            unconcat_tokens, total_lengths, response_lengths, strict=False
        ):
            chunk_size_cp, chunks_offset, logits_offset, tokens_offset = get_logits_and_tokens_offset_with_cp(
                total_length, response_length
            )
            for half, base in ((0, end), (1, end + chunk_size_cp)):
                lo = logits_offset[half][0] - chunks_offset[half][0]
                hi = logits_offset[half][1] - chunks_offset[half][0]
                full_tokens[base + lo : base + hi] = tokens[tokens_offset[half][0] : tokens_offset[half][1]]
            end += 2 * chunk_size_cp
        return full_tokens

127	    """

136	    cp_size = mpu.get_context_parallel_world_size()
137	    end = 0
138	    seq_start = 0
139	    for tokens, total_length, response_length in zip(unconcat_tokens, total_lengths, response_lengths, strict=False):

153	            prompt_length = total_length - response_length

157	            logit_global_end = resp_token_end - 1

183	            assert logits_0.size(0) == tokens_0.size(0), f"{logits_0.size(0)} vs {tokens_0.size(0)}"

187	            tokens_chunk = torch.cat([tokens_0, tokens_1], dim=0)

194	def _allgather_cp_redistribute(
195	    res: dict[str, list[torch.Tensor]],
196	    *,
197	    logits_local_len: int,
198	    total_lengths: list[int],
199	    response_lengths: list[int],
200	) -> None:
201	    """Redistribute response tensors from allgather-CP layout to zigzag ring-attn layout.
202	
203	    After allgather context parallelism, each rank holds a contiguous chunk of
204	    the global sequence.  This helper reconstructs per-sample full response
205	    tensors via a differentiable all-reduce and re-slices them into the zigzag
206	    CP pattern expected by downstream code.
207	
208	    The *res* dict is modified **in-place**.
209	
210	    Args:
211	        res: Dict mapping metric names to lists of per-sample tensors.
212	        logits_local_len: Local sequence length on this rank.
213	        total_lengths: Total sequence lengths (prompt + response) per sample.
214	        response_lengths: Response segment lengths per sample.
215	    """
216	    cp_group = mpu.get_context_parallel_group()
217	    cp_rank = mpu.get_context_parallel_rank()
218	    chunk_start = cp_rank * logits_local_len
219	    chunk_end = chunk_start + logits_local_len
220	
221	    for key, values in res.items():
222	        # Skip keys where all values are None (e.g. entropy when not computed)
223	        if all(v is None for v in values):
224	            continue
225	
226	        # Determine reference dtype/device from first non-None value
227	        ref_value = next(v for v in values if v is not None)
228	        ref_dtype = ref_value.dtype
229	        ref_device = ref_value.device
230	
231	        # Reconstruct full response tensors with each rank's contiguous contribution
232	        full_resps = []
233	        seq_start = 0
234	        for value, total_length, response_length in zip(values, total_lengths, response_lengths, strict=False):
235	            prompt_length = total_length - response_length
236	            logit_global_start = seq_start + prompt_length - 1
237	            logit_global_end = seq_start + total_length - 1
238	
239	            s = max(logit_global_start, chunk_start)
240	            e = min(logit_global_end, chunk_end)
241	
242	            if value is None or e <= s:
243	                # This rank has no response logprobs for this sample
244	                full_resp = torch.zeros(
245	                    response_length,
246	                    dtype=ref_dtype,
247	                    device=ref_device,
248	                    requires_grad=ref_value.requires_grad,
249	                )
250	            else:
251	                resp_start = s - logit_global_start
252	                resp_end = e - logit_global_start
253	                full_resp = F.pad(value, (resp_start, response_length - resp_end))
254	
255	            assert full_resp.size(0) == response_length, f"Expected {response_length}, got {full_resp.size(0)}"
256	            full_resps.append(full_resp)
257	            seq_start += total_length
258	
259	        # Single differentiable all-reduce to gather full response from all CP ranks.
260	        all_cat = torch.cat(full_resps, dim=0)
261	        all_cat = dist.nn.all_reduce(all_cat, group=cp_group)
262	
263	        # Re-slice each sample into zigzag CP pattern
264	        new_values = []
265	        for full_resp, total_length, response_length in zip(
266	            all_cat.split(response_lengths, dim=0), total_lengths, response_lengths, strict=False
267	        ):
268	            new_values.append(slice_log_prob_with_cp(full_resp, total_length, response_length))
269	
270	        res[key] = new_values
271

274	    T: int,
275	    device: torch.device,
276	    unconcat_tokens: list[torch.Tensor],
277	    total_lengths: list[int],
278	    response_lengths: list[int],
279	    allgather_cp: bool,
280	) -> torch.Tensor:
281	    """Build shifted target tokens for the full packed/padded logits."""
282	    cp_size = mpu.get_context_parallel_world_size()
283	
284	    # --- zigzag CP: completely different layout ---
285	    if cp_size > 1 and not allgather_cp:
286	        full_tokens = torch.zeros(T, dtype=torch.long, device=device)
287	        end = 0
288	        for tokens, total_length, response_length in zip(
289	            unconcat_tokens, total_lengths, response_lengths, strict=False
290	        ):
291	            chunk_size_cp, chunks_offset, logits_offset, tokens_offset = get_logits_and_tokens_offset_with_cp(
292	                total_length, response_length
293	            )
294	            for half, base in ((0, end), (1, end + chunk_size_cp)):
295	                lo = logits_offset[half][0] - chunks_offset[half][0]
296	                hi = logits_offset[half][1] - chunks_offset[half][0]
297	                full_tokens[base + lo : base + hi] = tokens[tokens_offset[half][0] : tokens_offset[half][1]]
298	            end += 2 * chunk_size_cp
299	        return full_tokens

301	    # --- cp1 and allgather-CP both build global shifted tokens the same way ---
302	    T_global = sum(total_lengths) if allgather_cp else T
303	    full_tokens = torch.zeros(T_global, dtype=torch.long, device=device)
304	
305	    offset = 0
306	    for tokens, total_length in zip(unconcat_tokens, total_lengths, strict=False):
307	        full_tokens[offset : offset + total_length - 1] = tokens[1:total_length]
308	        offset += total_length
309	
310	    # allgather-CP: slice to local chunk
311	    if allgather_cp:
312	        cp_rank = mpu.get_context_parallel_rank()
313	        chunk_start = cp_rank * T
314	        chunk_end = chunk_start + T
315	        if chunk_end <= T_global:
316	            return full_tokens[chunk_start:chunk_end].contiguous()
317	        local = torch.zeros(T, dtype=torch.long, device=device)
318	        valid = T_global - chunk_start
319	        if valid > 0:
320	            local[:valid] = full_tokens[chunk_start:]
321	        return local

326	def _fill_topp_mask_rows(
327	    keep: torch.Tensor,
328	    ids: list[int],
329	    offsets: list[int],
330	    response_start: int,
331	    local_start: int,
332	    length: int,
333	    vocab_start: int,
334	    vocab_end: int,
335	) -> None:
336	    end = min(response_start + length, max(len(offsets) - 1, 0))
337	    for response_idx in range(response_start, end):
338	        local_ids = [
339	            token_id - vocab_start
340	            for token_id in ids[offsets[response_idx] : offsets[response_idx + 1]]
341	            if vocab_start <= token_id < vocab_end
342	        ]
343	        row = local_start + response_idx - response_start
344	        keep[row].fill_(False)
345	        if local_ids:
346	            keep[row, torch.tensor(local_ids, device=keep.device, dtype=torch.long)] = True

349	def _build_topp_keep_mask(
350	    T: int,
351	    vocab_local: int,
352	    device: torch.device,
353	    top_p_token_ids: list[list[int]],
354	    top_p_token_offsets: list[list[int]],
355	    total_lengths: list[int],
356	    response_lengths: list[int],
357	    allgather_cp: bool,
358	) -> torch.Tensor:
359	    """Build a ``[T, vocab_local]`` boolean keep-mask aligned to local logits.
360	
361	    For response token ``r`` of a sample, the rollout top-p nucleus is
362	    ``ids[offsets[r]:offsets[r + 1]]``. Rows without a recorded nucleus stay
363	    all-True, so only response rows with replay data are masked.
364	    """
365	    cp_size = mpu.get_context_parallel_world_size()
366	    tp_rank = mpu.get_tensor_model_parallel_rank()
367	    vocab_start = tp_rank * vocab_local
368	    vocab_end = vocab_start + vocab_local
369	
370	    # Normalize ragged payloads (may arrive as CPU int32 tensors) to python lists.
371	    top_p_token_ids = [t.tolist() if torch.is_tensor(t) else list(t) for t in top_p_token_ids]
372	    top_p_token_offsets = [t.tolist() if torch.is_tensor(t) else list(t) for t in top_p_token_offsets]
373	
374	    keep = torch.ones((T, vocab_local), dtype=torch.bool, device=device)
375	
376	    if cp_size > 1 and not allgather_cp:
377	        local_base = 0
378	        for ids, offsets, total_length, response_length in zip(
379	            top_p_token_ids, top_p_token_offsets, total_lengths, response_lengths, strict=False
380	        ):
381	            prompt_length = total_length - response_length
382	            chunk_size_cp, chunks_offset, logits_offset, tokens_offset = get_logits_and_tokens_offset_with_cp(
383	                total_length, response_length
384	            )
385	            for half, base in ((0, local_base), (1, local_base + chunk_size_cp)):
386	                local_start = base + logits_offset[half][0] - chunks_offset[half][0]
387	                length = logits_offset[half][1] - logits_offset[half][0]
388	                response_start = tokens_offset[half][0] - prompt_length
389	                _fill_topp_mask_rows(keep, ids, offsets, response_start, local_start, length, vocab_start, vocab_end)
390	            local_base += 2 * chunk_size_cp
391	        return keep
392	
393	    if allgather_cp:
394	        cp_rank = mpu.get_context_parallel_rank()
395	        chunk_start = cp_rank * T
396	        chunk_end = chunk_start + T
397	        seq_start = 0
398	        for ids, offsets, total_length, response_length in zip(
399	            top_p_token_ids, top_p_token_offsets, total_lengths, response_lengths, strict=False
400	        ):
401	            prompt_length = total_length - response_length
402	            logit_global_start = seq_start + prompt_length - 1
403	            logit_global_end = seq_start + total_length - 1
404	            s = max(logit_global_start, chunk_start)
405	            e = min(logit_global_end, chunk_end)
406	            if e > s:
407	                _fill_topp_mask_rows(
408	                    keep,
409	                    ids,
410	                    offsets,
411	                    s - logit_global_start,
412	                    s - chunk_start,
413	                    e - s,
414	                    vocab_start,
415	                    vocab_end,
416	                )
417	            seq_start += total_length
418	        return keep
419	
420	    offset = 0
421	    for ids, offsets, total_length, response_length in zip(
422	        top_p_token_ids, top_p_token_offsets, total_lengths, response_lengths, strict=False
423	    ):
424	        end = offset + total_length
425	        start = end - response_length
426	        _fill_topp_mask_rows(keep, ids, offsets, 0, start - 1, response_length, vocab_start, vocab_end)
427	        offset += total_length
428	
429	    return keep

432	def _extract_per_sample(
433	    log_prob_full: torch.Tensor,
434	    entropy_full: torch.Tensor | None,
435	    total_lengths: list[int],
436	    response_lengths: list[int],
437	    allgather_cp: bool,
438	) -> tuple[list[torch.Tensor], list[torch.Tensor | None]]:
439	    """Slice per-sample response log-probs/entropy from full-length 1-D tensors."""
440	    cp_size = mpu.get_context_parallel_world_size()
441	    log_probs_list: list[torch.Tensor] = []
442	    entropy_list: list[torch.Tensor] = []
443	
444	    if cp_size > 1 and not allgather_cp:
445	        # zigzag CP
446	        pos = 0
447	        for total_length, response_length in zip(total_lengths, response_lengths, strict=False):
448	            chunk_size_cp, chunks_offset, logits_offset, _tokens_offset = get_logits_and_tokens_offset_with_cp(
449	                total_length, response_length
450	            )
451	            lo0 = logits_offset[0][0] - chunks_offset[0][0]
452	            hi0 = logits_offset[0][1] - chunks_offset[0][0]
453	            lo1 = logits_offset[1][0] - chunks_offset[1][0]
454	            hi1 = logits_offset[1][1] - chunks_offset[1][0]
455	
456	            lp = torch.cat(
457	                [
458	                    log_prob_full[pos + lo0 : pos + hi0],
459	                    log_prob_full[pos + chunk_size_cp + lo1 : pos + chunk_size_cp + hi1],
460	                ],
461	                dim=0,
462	            )
463	            log_probs_list.append(lp)
464	            if entropy_full is not None:
465	                ent = torch.cat(
466	                    [
467	                        entropy_full[pos + lo0 : pos + hi0],
468	                        entropy_full[pos + chunk_size_cp + lo1 : pos + chunk_size_cp + hi1],
469	                    ],
470	                    dim=0,
471	                )
472	                entropy_list.append(ent)
473	            pos += 2 * chunk_size_cp
474	
475	    elif allgather_cp:
476	        cp_rank = mpu.get_context_parallel_rank()
477	        local_len = log_prob_full.size(0)
478	        chunk_start = cp_rank * local_len
479	        chunk_end = chunk_start + local_len
480	
481	        seq_start = 0
482	        for total_length, response_length in zip(total_lengths, response_lengths, strict=False):
483	            prompt_length = total_length - response_length
484	            logit_global_start = seq_start + prompt_length - 1
485	            logit_global_end = seq_start + total_length - 1
486	
487	            s = max(logit_global_start, chunk_start)
488	            e = min(logit_global_end, chunk_end)
489	            if e <= s:
490	                log_probs_list.append(log_prob_full[:0])
491	                if entropy_full is not None:
492	                    entropy_list.append(entropy_full[:0])
493	            else:
494	                log_probs_list.append(log_prob_full[s - chunk_start : e - chunk_start])
495	                if entropy_full is not None:
496	                    entropy_list.append(entropy_full[s - chunk_start : e - chunk_start])
497	            seq_start += total_length
498	
499	    else:
500	        # cp1
501	        offset = 0
502	        for total_length, response_length in zip(total_lengths, response_lengths, strict=False):
503	            end = offset + total_length
504	            start = end - response_length
505	            log_probs_list.append(log_prob_full[start - 1 : end - 1])
506	            if entropy_full is not None:

513	def get_log_probs_and_entropy(
514	    logits: torch.Tensor,
515	    *,
516	    args: Namespace,
517	    unconcat_tokens: list[torch.Tensor],
518	    total_lengths: list[int],
519	    response_lengths: list[int],
520	    with_entropy: bool = False,
521	    non_loss_data: bool = True,
522	    top_p_token_ids: list[list[int]] | None = None,
523	    top_p_token_offsets: list[list[int]] | None = None,
524	) -> dict[str, list[torch.Tensor]]:
525	    """Compute per-token log-probabilities (and optionally entropy) on responses.
526	
527	    Computes on the **full** logits ``[T, V]`` tensor at once (instead of
528	    per-sample slicing) so backward traverses ``[T, V]`` only once, then
529	    extracts per-sample response portions.
530	
531	    If rollout top-p replay is provided, the keep-mask is applied only to
532	    log-probabilities; entropy is always computed from the unmasked logits.
533	    """
534	    assert non_loss_data
535	    assert logits.dtype == torch.float32, f"{logits.dtype}"
536	    assert len(logits.shape) == 3, f"{logits.shape}"
537	    assert logits.size(0) == 1, f"{logits.shape}"
538	    logits = logits.squeeze(0)
539	
540	    # Apply rollout temperature scaling to logits to match rollout-time log-probs.
541	    rollout_temperature = getattr(args, "rollout_temperature", 1.0)
542	    if rollout_temperature != 1.0:
543	        logits = logits / rollout_temperature
544	    logits = logits.contiguous()
545	    T = logits.size(0)
546	    device = logits.device
547	    tp_group = mpu.get_tensor_model_parallel_group()
548	    chunk_size = args.log_probs_chunk_size
549	    # Keep entropy metrics, but skip saving entropy-backward activations when
550	    # the entropy term cannot affect the loss.
551	    with_entropy_grad = with_entropy and getattr(args, "entropy_coef", 0.0) != 0
552	
553	    # --- build full shifted-token target tensor ---
554	    full_tokens = _build_shifted_tokens(T, device, unconcat_tokens, total_lengths, response_lengths, args.allgather_cp)
555	
556	    # --- build top-p nucleus keep-mask (logprob only; entropy stays unmasked) ---
557	    top_p_keep_mask = None
558	    if top_p_token_ids is not None and top_p_token_offsets is not None:
559	        top_p_keep_mask = _build_topp_keep_mask(
560	            T,
561	            logits.size(-1),
562	            device,
563	            top_p_token_ids,
564	            top_p_token_offsets,
565	            total_lengths,
566	            response_lengths,
567	            args.allgather_cp,
568	        )
569	
570	    # --- compute on full [T,V] logits at once via calculate_log_probs_and_entropy ---
571	    log_prob_full, entropy_full = calculate_log_probs_and_entropy(
572	        logits,
573	        full_tokens,
574	        tp_group,
575	        with_entropy=with_entropy,
576	        with_entropy_grad=with_entropy_grad,
577	        chunk_size=chunk_size,
578	        log_prob_keep_mask=top_p_keep_mask,
579	    )
580	    log_prob_full = log_prob_full.squeeze(-1)  # [T, 1] -> [T]
581	
582	    # --- extract per-sample response portions ---
583	    log_probs_list, entropy_list = _extract_per_sample(
584	        log_prob_full,
585	        entropy_full,
586	        total_lengths,
587	        response_lengths,
588	        args.allgather_cp,
589	    )
590	
591	    res = {"log_probs": log_probs_list}
592	    if with_entropy:
593	        res["entropy"] = entropy_list
594	
595	    # we need to turn the all gather kv into zigzag ring attn kv
596	    if args.allgather_cp:
597	        _allgather_cp_redistribute(
598	            res,
599	            logits_local_len=T,
600	            total_lengths=total_lengths,
601	            response_lengths=response_lengths,
602	        )
603	
604	    return torch.empty((0,), device=device), res

607	def get_values(
608	    logits: torch.Tensor,
609	    *,
610	    args: Namespace,
611	    unconcat_tokens: list[torch.Tensor],
612	    total_lengths: list[int],
613	    response_lengths: list[int],
614	    with_entropy: bool = False,
615	    non_loss_data: bool = True,
616	) -> dict[str, list[torch.Tensor]]:
617	    """Extract per-token value predictions over response tokens.
618	
619	    For each sample, extracts response-aligned chunks from the value head
620	    output and squeezes the final dimension from `[R, 1]` to `[R]`.
621	
622	    Args:
623	        logits: Value head output with shape `[1, T, 1]`.
624	        args: Configuration passed to `get_responses`; temperature scaling is
625	            disabled for value outputs.
626	        unconcat_tokens: List of token tensors per sample.
627	        total_lengths: Total sequence lengths per sample.
628	        response_lengths: Response segment lengths per sample.
629	        with_entropy: Unused; kept for signature compatibility.
630	        non_loss_data: Unused; kept for signature compatibility.
631	
632	    Returns:
633	        Dict with key "values" mapping to a list of `[R]` value tensors
634	        per sample.
635	    """
636	    value_list = []
637	    for logits_chunk, _ in get_responses(
638	        logits,
639	        args=args,
640	        unconcat_tokens=unconcat_tokens,
641	        total_lengths=total_lengths,
642	        response_lengths=response_lengths,
643	        apply_temperature=False,
644	    ):
645	        assert logits_chunk.size(-1) == 1, f"{logits_chunk.shape}"
646	        value_list.append(logits_chunk.squeeze(-1))
647	
648	    res = {

# --- cp1 and allgather-CP both build global shifted tokens the same way ---
    T_global = sum(total_lengths) if allgather_cp else T
    full_tokens = torch.zeros(T_global, dtype=torch.long, device=device)

    offset = 0
    for tokens, total_length in zip(unconcat_tokens, total_lengths, strict=False):
        full_tokens[offset : offset + total_length - 1] = tokens[1:total_length]
        offset += total_length

    # allgather-CP: slice to local chunk
    if allgather_cp:
        cp_rank = mpu.get_context_parallel_rank()
        chunk_start = cp_rank * T
        chunk_end = chunk_start + T
        if chunk_end <= T_global:
            return full_tokens[chunk_start:chunk_end].contiguous()
        local = torch.zeros(T, dtype=torch.long, device=device)
        valid = T_global - chunk_start
        if valid > 0:
            local[:valid] = full_tokens[chunk_start:]
        return local

    return full_tokens


def _fill_topp_mask_rows(
    keep: torch.Tensor,
    ids: list[int],
    offsets: list[int],
    response_start: int,
    local_start: int,
    length: int,
    vocab_start: int,
    vocab_end: int,
) -> None:
    end = min(response_start + length, max(len(offsets) - 1, 0))
    for response_idx in range(response_start, end):
        local_ids = [
            token_id - vocab_start
            for token_id in ids[offsets[response_idx] : offsets[response_idx + 1]]
            if vocab_start <= token_id < vocab_end
        ]
        row = local_start + response_idx - response_start
        keep[row].fill_(False)
        if local_ids:
            keep[row, torch.tensor(local_ids, device=keep.device, dtype=torch.long)] = True


def _build_topp_keep_mask(
    T: int,
    vocab_local: int,
    device: torch.device,
    top_p_token_ids: list[list[int]],
    top_p_token_offsets: list[list[int]],
    total_lengths: list[int],
    response_lengths: list[int],
    allgather_cp: bool,
) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Build a ``[T, vocab_local]`` boolean keep-mask aligned to local logits.

    For response token ``r`` of a sample, the rollout top-p nucleus is
    ``ids[offsets[r]:offsets[r + 1]]``. Rows without a recorded nucleus stay
    all-True, so only response rows with replay data are masked.
    """
    cp_size = mpu.get_context_parallel_world_size()
    tp_rank = mpu.get_tensor_model_parallel_rank()
    vocab_start = tp_rank * vocab_local
    vocab_end = vocab_start + vocab_local

    # Normalize ragged payloads (may arrive as CPU int32 tensors) to python lists.
    top_p_token_ids = [t.tolist() if torch.is_tensor(t) else list(t) for t in top_p_token_ids]
    top_p_token_offsets = [t.tolist() if torch.is_tensor(t) else list(t) for t in top_p_token_offsets]

    keep = torch.ones((T, vocab_local), dtype=torch.bool, device=device)

    if cp_size > 1 and not allgather_cp:
        local_base = 0
        for ids, offsets, total_length, response_length in zip(
            top_p_token_ids, top_p_token_offsets, total_lengths, response_lengths, strict=False
        ):
            prompt_length = total_length - response_length
            chunk_size_cp, chunks_offset, logits_offset, tokens_offset = get_logits_and_tokens_offset_with_cp(
                total_length, response_length
            )
            for half, base in ((0, local_base), (1, local_base + chunk_size_cp)):
                local_start = base + logits_offset[half][0] - chunks_offset[half][0]
                length = logits_offset[half][1] - logits_offset[half][0]
                response_start = tokens_offset[half][0] - prompt_length
                _fill_topp_mask_rows(keep, ids, offsets, response_start, local_start, length, vocab_start, vocab_end)
            local_base += 2 * chunk_size_cp
        return keep

    if allgather_cp:
        cp_rank = mpu.get_context_parallel_rank()
        chunk_start = cp_rank * T
        chunk_end = chunk_start + T
        seq_start = 0
        for ids, offsets, total_length, response_length in zip(
            top_p_token_ids, top_p_token_offsets, total_lengths, response_lengths, strict=False
        ):
            prompt_length = total_length - response_length
            logit_global_start = seq_start + prompt_length - 1
            logit_global_end = seq_start + total_length - 1
            s = max(logit_global_start, chunk_start)
            e = min(logit_global_end, chunk_end)
            if e > s:
                _fill_topp_mask_rows(
                    keep,
                    ids,
                    offsets,
                    s - logit_global_start,
                    s - chunk_start,
                    e - s,
                    vocab_start,
                    vocab_end,
                )
            seq_start += total_length
        return keep

    offset = 0
    for ids, offsets, total_length, response_length in zip(
        top_p_token_ids, top_p_token_offsets, total_lengths, response_lengths, strict=False
    ):
        end = offset + total_length
        start = end - response_length
        _fill_topp_mask_rows(keep, ids, offsets, 0, start - 1, response_length, vocab_start, vocab_end)
        offset += total_length

    return keep


def _extract_per_sample(
    log_prob_full: torch.Tensor,
    entropy_full: torch.Tensor | None,
    total_lengths: list[int],
    response_lengths: list[int],
    allgather_cp: bool,
) -> tuple[list[torch.Tensor], list[torch.Tensor | None]]:
    """Slice per-sample response log-probs/entropy from full-length 1-D tensors."""
    cp_size = mpu.get_context_parallel_world_size()
    log_probs_list: list[torch.Tensor] = []
    entropy_list: list[torch.Tensor] = []

    if cp_size > 1 and not allgather_cp:
        # zigzag CP
        pos = 0
        for total_length, response_length in zip(total_lengths, response_lengths, strict=False):
            chunk_size_cp, chunks_offset, logits_offset, _tokens_offset = get_logits_and_tokens_offset_with_cp(
                total_length, response_length
            )
            lo0 = logits_offset[0][0] - chunks_offset[0][0]
            hi0 = logits_offset[0][1] - chunks_offset[0][0]
            lo1 = logits_offset[1][0] - chunks_offset[1][0]
            hi1 = logits_offset[1][1] - chunks_offset[1][0]

            lp = torch.cat(
                [
                    log_prob_full[pos + lo0 : pos + hi0],
                    log_prob_full[pos + chunk_size_cp + lo1 : pos + chunk_size_cp + hi1],
                ],
                dim=0,
            )
            log_probs_list.append(lp)
            if entropy_full is not None:
                ent = torch.cat(
                    [
                        entropy_full[pos + lo0 : pos + hi0],
                        entropy_full[pos + chunk_size_cp + lo1 : pos + chunk_size_cp + hi1],
                    ],
                    dim=0,
                )
                entropy_list.append(ent)
            pos += 2 * chunk_size_cp

    elif allgather_cp:
        cp_rank = mpu.get_context_parallel_rank()
        local_len = log_prob_full.size(0)
        chunk_start = cp_rank * local_len
        chunk_end = chunk_start + local_len

        seq_start = 0
        for total_length, response_length in zip(total_lengths, response_lengths, strict=False):
            prompt_length = total_length - response_length
            logit_global_start = seq_start + prompt_length - 1
            logit_global_end = seq_start + total_length - 1

            s = max(logit_global_start, chunk_start)
            e = min(logit_global_end, chunk_end)
            if e <= s:
                log_probs_list.append(log_prob_full[:0])
                if entropy_full is not None:
                    entropy_list.append(entropy_full[:0])
            else:
                log_probs_list.append(log_prob_full[s - chunk_start : e - chunk_start])
                if entropy_full is not None:
                    entropy_list.append(entropy_full[s - chunk_start : e - chunk_start])
            seq_start += total_length

    else:
        # cp1
        offset = 0
        for total_length, response_length in zip(total_lengths, response_lengths, strict=False):
            end = offset + total_length
            start = end - response_length
            log_probs_list.append(log_prob_full[start - 1 : end - 1])
            if entropy_full is not None:
                entropy_list.append(entropy_full[start - 1 : end - 1])
            offset += total_length

    return log_probs_list, entropy_list


def get_log_probs_and_entropy(
    logits: torch.Tensor,
    *,
    args: Namespace,
    unconcat_tokens: list[torch.Tensor],
    total_lengths: list[int],
    response_lengths: list[int],
    with_entropy: bool = False,
    non_loss_data: bool = True,
    top_p_token_ids: list[list[int]] | None = None,
    top_p_token_offsets: list[list[int]] | None = None,
) -> dict[str, list[torch.Tensor]]:
    """Compute per-token log-probabilities (and optionally entropy) on responses.

    Computes on the **full** logits ``[T, V]`` tensor at once (instead of
    per-sample slicing) so backward traverses ``[T, V]`` only once, then
    extracts per-sample response portions.

    If rollout top-p replay is provided, the keep-mask is applied only to
    log-probabilities; entropy is always computed from the unmasked logits.
    """
    assert non_loss_data
    assert logits.dtype == torch.float32, f"{logits.dtype}"
    assert len(logits.shape) == 3, f"{logits.shape}"
    assert logits.size(0) == 1, f"{logits.shape}"
    logits = logits.squeeze(0)

    # Apply rollout temperature scaling to logits to match rollout-time log-probs.
    rollout_temperature = getattr(args, "rollout_temperature", 1.0)
    if rollout_temperature != 1.0:
        logits = logits / rollout_temperature
    logits = logits.contiguous()
    T = logits.size(0)
    device = logits.device
    tp_group = mpu.get_tensor_model_parallel_group()
    chunk_size = args.log_probs_chunk_size
    # Keep entropy metrics, but skip saving entropy-backward activations when
    # the entropy term cannot affect the loss.
    with_entropy_grad = with_entropy and getattr(args, "entropy_coef", 0.0) != 0

    # --- build full shifted-token target tensor ---
    full_tokens = _build_shifted_tokens(T, device, unconcat_tokens, total_lengths, response_lengths, args.allgather_cp)

    # --- build top-p nucleus keep-mask (logprob only; entropy stays unmasked) ---
    top_p_keep_mask = None
    if top_p_token_ids is not None and top_p_token_offsets is not None:
        top_p_keep_mask = _build_topp_keep_mask(
            T,
            logits.size(-1),
            device,
            top_p_token_ids,
            top_p_token_offsets,
